title: Enterprise Onboarding: Integrations, Known Issues, Escalation, and QBR Playbook
author: Jordan Kim
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates the standard approach for enterprise onboarding at Redwood Inference with a focus on integrations (API & webhook), common known issues and workarounds, the escalation matrix and runbooks, and the Quarterly Business Review (QBR) / health-check materials. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering (SE), Support, and SRE collaborators.

Scope
- Applies to enterprise customers (Dedicated and Private deployments) during Trial -> Onboarding -> Go-live -> First 90 days of production.
- Covers pre-integration checks, integration validation, common upgrade/compatibility problems and mitigations, and escalation steps for P0/P1 incidents.

Responsibilities
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): overall onboarding owner, QBR lead, customer communication.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): integration configuration, API/webhook verification, sample app support.
- Support (Triage team): ticket intake and initial troubleshooting, escalate per matrix.
- SRE/Platform: incident response for platform-level issues (capacity, SLO breaches).

Pre-Onboarding Checklist (to complete before integration kick-off)
1. Contract & access validated: account IDs, billing, and required NDAs shared.
2. Network requirements confirmed: VPC peering, egress IPs, TLS termination, KMS/HSM access (if Private).
3. Test dataset & acceptance criteria defined (latency, throughput, correctness).
4. Contact matrix: CSM, SE, technical POC, network/security POC, and escalation phone numbers.

Integration Guide (API + Webhooks)
- API Access
  - Create an API key for the customer in the Console -> Integrations -> API Keys. Use restricted keys for test/dev environments.
  - Example generation request (curl):

    curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
      -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" 
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
      -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-2.1", "input":"Summarize the following...", "max_tokens":256}'

  - For high-throughput integrations, configure a connection pool and enable batching in the SDK. Recommended default batching window: 10ms.

- Webhooks
  - Webhooks are configured in Console -> Integrations -> Webhooks. Required fields: endpoint URL, secret (HMAC SHA256), event types (generation.complete, job.failed, usage.alerts).
  - Example verification header: X-Redwood-Signature: sha256=...
  - SEs should validate replay protection (timestamp tolerance 60s) and log raw webhook payloads to S3 for debugging.

Integration Validation Matrix (minimum tests)
- Auth: 401/403 handled gracefully; key rotation test passed.
- Latency: median request < 150ms (hosted) / per-customer SLA for Dedicated.
- Throughput: sustained 100 req/s with 95th token latency within targets (adjust per contract).
- Error handling: 429/503 backoff and retry policy verified.

Configuration Table (example settings)
- model: rw-instruct-2.1
- max_tokens: 512
- temperature: 0.0-0.8 (recommended 0.0 for deterministic eval)
- batch_window_ms: 10
- kv_cache_sharing: enabled for session-based workloads

Onboarding Timeline (example 4-week plan)
1. Week 0: Kickoff, network checks, access.
2. Week 1: SE-led integration and smoke tests.
3. Week 2: Performance tuning (batching, quantization suggestions), run load tests.
4. Week 3: Cutover rehearsal, fallback policy validation.
5. Week 4: Go-live, health checks, QBR scheduling

Escalation Playbook
- Severity definitions and target response/RTTs:
  - P0 (Platform outage / company-wide outage): Response 15m, mitigation plan in 30m, owner: SRE oncall.
  - P1 (Customer-impacting degraded performance / data loss possibility): Response 1h, mitigation in 4h, owner: Support lead + SE.
  - P2 (Partial feature outage / non-critical regressions): Response 4h, owner: Support.
  - P3 (Minor issues / request for enhancement): Response 1 business day, owner: CSM/Support.

- Escalation matrix (first 24 hours)
  1. Triage team assigns priority and performs initial diagnosis (logs, request IDs, customer context).
  2. If P0/P1, open an incident in the incident system and page SRE and SE. Use Slack channel #incidents and include: customer name, impacted routes, request IDs, sample logs, timeline.
  3. SE performs customer-facing troubleshooting and recommends temporary mitigations (route to model variant, reduce concurrency, enable cache).
  4. If issue is due to customer configuration (network, client), assign SE/CSM to coordinate fix.
  5. For platform bugs, SRE owns remediation, coordinates deploy/rollback, and provides ETA.

Triage Runbook: Step-by-step for P1
1. Gather context: customer ID, request IDs, timestamps, deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), region, model.
2. Check platform SLOs & dashboard (Console -> Dashboards -> Per-customer latency & error rate).
3. Reproduce with a minimal curl request; capture server response, headers, and raw logs.
4. If reproducible, collect a trace and escalate to SRE with trace link and label "customer-impacting".
5. Communicate interim mitigation to customer and CSM every 60 minutes until resolution.

Known Issues & Workarounds (selected)
- Issue: 503s during high-concurrency spikes on older runtime kernel
  - Symptom: intermittent generation failures with 503 and "kernel OOM" in logs.
  - Workaround: Route customer to kernel-v2 or reduce max_concurrency to 8; enable KV caching to reduce repeated context.

- Issue: Webhook payloads dropped by corporate firewalls
  - Symptom: Customer reports no webhook events, webhook delivery status shows 4xx/timeout.
  - Workaround: Ask customer to whitelist Redwood webhook IP range (see Console -> Integrations -> Webhook IPs). Recommend using a forwarding endpoint or AWS SNS if corporate firewall policies are strict.

- Issue: Tokenization differences in locally preprocessed input
  - Symptom: Mismatch between local evaluation and server output, off-by-one tokens on truncation.
  - Workaround: Confirm model tokenizer version (rw-tokenizer v2.1) and use SDK's token_count() helper. Normalize whitespace and control characters before scoring.

Support Process & Communication Templates
- Ticketing flow: Zendesk -> Triage -> Assign/Label {customer_enterprise} -> If P1+, create incident ticket and link to channel.
- Required ticket fields: customer_id, deployment_type, severity, reproduction steps, sample request IDs, logs (redacted).
- Customer status updates:
  - Initial acknowledgement: within response SLA.
  - Interim updates: every 60 minutes for P1, every 4 hours for P2.
  - Post-resolution summary: root cause, remediation, and timeline of events.

QBR & Health Check Materials
- Standard QBR agenda (60 min)
  1. Introductions and objectives (5m)
  2. Usage & cost trends (10m)
  3. Performance: latency, error rates, tail latency (10m)
  4. Reliability: incidents, mitigations, upcoming changes (10m)
  5. Optimization opportunities: batching, model variants, quantization (10m)
  6. Roadmap & feature requests (10m)
  7. Action items and next steps (5m)

- Health check metrics (minimum)
  - Availability (SLO target: 99.9% monthly)
  - Median / 95th / 99th token latency by route
  - Error rate (4xx vs 5xx) and root cause split
  - Cost per 1k tokens and high-cost patterns
  - Model quality regressions (tie to eval prompt sets)

QBR Deliverables
- Slide deck template (attachable): executive summary, metrics, incidents, recommendations, action items.
- Action tracker: Jira board or shared Google Sheet with owners and due dates.

Go-live & Post-Go-live Checklist
- Verify production API keys and rotate test keys.
- Confirm monitoring alerts configured (latency threshold, error rate > 0.5%).
- Run a 1-hour soak test at expected production load.
- Schedule 1-week and 30-day health checks with CSM + SE.
